draft.title: Transforming parabolas
card: A parabola can be written as \(y = a(x - h)^{2} + k\). Its vertex, the turning point, is the point \((h, k)\).
Changing \(h\) moves the parabola sideways. Changing \(k\) moves it up or down. The shape stays the same.
The number \(a\) stretches or flips the parabola. If \(a\) is negative, it flips and is concave down. If \(a\) is positive, it is concave up.
Example: \(y = -(x - 3)^{2} + 2\) has \(h = 3\), \(k = 2\) and \(a = -1\). Its vertex is \((3, 2)\) and it is concave down. Note that \(x - 3\) gives \(h = 3\), not \(-3\).

4.alt: The parabola \(y = -(x - 3)^{2} + 2\), concave down, with its vertex at \((3, 2)\).

draft.remember: In \(y = a(x - h)^{2} + k\), read the vertex \((h, k)\) and use \(a\) to see the flip.

a.why: The equation matches \(y = a(x - h)^{2} + k\) with \(h = 4\) and \(k = 5\), so the vertex is \((4, 5)\). The option \((-4, 5)\) is tempting because of the minus sign, but \(x - 4\) means \(h = 4\).
a.clue: Match the equation to \(a(x - h)^{2} + k\) and read \(h\) and \(k\).

b.q: The parabola \(y = x^{2}\) is changed to \(y = -(x + 2)^{2} - 3\). Which describes the change?
opts: Flipped, then moved 2 left and 3 down
Flipped, then moved 2 right and 3 down
Flipped, then moved 2 left and 3 up
Not flipped, moved 2 left and 3 down
b.why: The negative sign makes \(a = -1\), so it flips. Writing \(x + 2\) as \(x - (-2)\) gives \(h = -2\), which is 2 left, and \(k = -3\) is 3 down. Moving 2 right is the common mistake of reading the sign of \(h\) the wrong way.
b.clue: Find the vertex \((h, k)\), then check the sign of \(a\).
